description:
FILED s536c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while building #1611's guard rows.  PRE-EXISTING (c950ad43); #1611 kept the keyword half of the call-site rule unchanged on purpose.

`Pl::PExpr::Config::is_core_keyword` asks `prototype("CORE::NAME")`, which answers for `say`, `fc`, `isa`, `evalbytes`, `break`, `__SUB__` ... whether or not the FEATURE that makes them keywords is in force at the call site.  Without `use feature 'say'` (or a `use v5.10`+ bundle) `say` is an ordinary identifier in perl, so a user sub of that name is called:

    sub say { print "MYSAY(@_)\n" } say("x");
    sub fc  { "MYFC(@_)" }  print fc("AB"), "\n";
    sub isa { "MYISA(@_)" } print isa(1,2), "\n";
      perl 5.40.3:  MYSAY(x) / MYFC(AB) / MYISA(1 2)
      PCL:          x / ab / (an empty line)

FIX SHAPE (not built): the keyword answer for a feature-gated name must also ask whether the feature is enabled at the site -- the lexical feature state Parser2 already tracks for `signatures` / `try` (`_signatures_enabled_at`'s scope walk, #455) is the reading to reuse, not a second one.  The set of gated names is perl's own (`feature.pm`'s `%feature`), measured from the running perl like `is_core_keyword`, never listed.  Both the call-site naming (`Pl::ExprToCL::source_call_is_builtin`) and the parse (PExpr's arity table) read it.

=== DONE (s536g) ===
MEASURED first over the 2,047-file list: 116 call heads of say / fc / isa / evalbytes, 5 not under a feature region -- t/op/lc.t:33 (`no feature 'fc'`: perl dies "Undefined subroutine &main::fc"), t/op/universal.t:248 (`isa` with a glob-installed sub), and lib/Search/Dict.pm 83/98/120, whose `fc` comes from a BEGIN-time `'feature'->import('fc')` that no static reading sees -- so a plain "feature off = sub call" rule would have broken Search::Dict.  The rule is three-valued, in ONE function `Pl::Parser::gated_keyword_at`: feature ON (a `use feature` / `use VERSION` region, `feature_regions_of`) = the keyword; OFF by a `no feature` pragma = an ordinary identifier, the sub call declared or not; UNSAID (no region, or a `use VERSION` bundle without it) = the keyword unless a sub of the name is known (declared in the package, also below the site; or imported).  The gated set is measured (`Pl::PExpr::Config::keyword_feature`: a keyword whose name is a feature of the running perl's feature.pm -- class defer evalbytes fc isa say state try); `%FEATURE_SINCE` gains say 10, fc 15, evalbytes 15, isa 35 (read off %feature::feature_bundle); regions now record what spoke (`feature` vs `version`, element [4]); `feature_state_at` is the tri-state reader.  Readers: `Pl::ExprToCL::source_call_is_builtin` (cl_name gets the head token, the gate is a callback) and PExpr's implicit-`$_` default (`_gated_keyword_is_sub`); ExprToCL's `say` `$_` push skips a user call.  perl = tree on 25 probe lines (scratch/s536g/p/feat1-4.pl).  RESIDUE (not done): with a user `fc`, `fc 1, 2` (no parens) still takes the builtin's named-unary operand parse.  Guard Pl/t/runtime-name-hygiene-01.t rows 18-20 (fail on c8886b61).  Companion op/lc.t 2688/28 -> 2689/27 (row 7 "fc() throws an exception," left baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv by edit).  Commit be344b80.


=== CLOSED (s536 reviewing session, 2026-11-08 20:1x) === merged as MAIN-READY-83 f5ecb8fc (s536g, generation v2-13100). Review probes perl -> main 8f046c7a -> tree (scratchpad p536g/a b b2 c d.pl, 37 lines): tree = perl on every line; main died on -K 1 (`&main::(p-- ...)`), dropped `(cwd 1, 2)` and the three dynamic-method chains, and called the builtins for user subs say / fc / isa. Rows keyed on this task: none left (comp/parser.t 45, op/lc.t 7 and YAML-PP 54.glob.t left their baselines in the batch).
subject: A user sub named like a FEATURE-GATED keyword (`say`, `fc`, `isa`, ...) is never called without the feature: `sub say {...} say("x")` prints x, `sub fc` lowercases, `sub isa {...} isa(1,2)` prints nothing (silent wrong)
